o: Trace the compilation and interpretation processes.
Compare benefits and drawbacks for real situations.
c: A processor runs machine instructions. A translator converts source code written in a programming language so the computer can execute it.
A compiler translates the entire program before it is run and produces executable code. The executable can normally be run again without recompiling unchanged source.
An interpreter translates and executes the program during running, commonly one statement at a time. It usually has to be present each time the source is run.
Compilation is useful when a finished program runs repeatedly or is distributed. Interpretation can be useful when developing and testing; error feedback can appear at the statement being executed.

m.title: Model how compilation works
m.q: Explain TWO features of a compiler. [4 marks]
st: A programmer begins with source code: this is not normally directly executable by the CPU.
The compiler translates the whole source program before it runs [1], rather than executing each statement as it is processed [1].
The compiler produces executable machine code [1] that the CPU can run.
The executable can be run repeatedly without translating the unchanged source again [1].

w: Explain TWO reasons an interpreter might be useful while developing a program. [4 marks]

It translates and executes during running [1], allowing source code to be tested without producing a separate executable [1]. Errors can be reported at the statement reached [1], helping the programmer locate a fault [1].
Compare when a compiler and an interpreter translate code, and what happens when the program runs again. [4 marks]

A compiler translates the whole program before execution [1]; an interpreter translates and executes during running [1]. A compiled executable can normally run again without recompilation [1]; an interpreted program normally needs the interpreter each time [1].
An application is distributed to many school computers and run every day. Explain TWO benefits of compiling it before distribution. [4 marks]

The compiled executable can be distributed to run on the target platform [1], without each user needing the source-language interpreter [1]. The unchanged executable can be run many times [1], without repeating compilation on every launch [1].

e:
A compiler reports an error before the programmer can run a new program. Explain why translation is necessary and how the compiler helps find a problem. [4 marks]

Source: Original OCR J277-style practice question.

The CPU needs executable machine instructions [1], so source code must be translated [1]. The compiler attempts to translate the whole source [1] and reports errors found during compilation so the programmer can correct them [1].

A learner changes the source code of a small program many times while testing. Explain ONE benefit and ONE drawback of interpreting the program. [4 marks]

Source: Original OCR J277-style practice question.

An interpreter translates and executes during running [1], allowing the learner to test changed code without a separate compilation step [1]. The interpreter is required at each run [1], which may make repeated execution slower than running a compiled executable [1].

A game studio wants users to run a finished game repeatedly on their own computers. Explain TWO advantages of compiling the game. [4 marks]

Source: Original OCR J277-style practice question.

The whole program is translated into executable code [1], so the distributed version can run on the target system [1]. The executable can run repeatedly [1], so recompilation of unchanged source is not needed each time [1].

r: State which language level is generally easier for people to read and maintain. [1 mark]
For Q=(A AND B) OR C, give Q when A=1, B=1, C=0. [2 marks]
Explain why low-level machine instructions are processor-dependent. [2 marks]
Different processors can have different instruction sets [1], so instructions for one CPU may not execute on another [1].
A school wants code that staff can change frequently and use on different processor families. Choose a language level and justify TWO advantages. [4 marks]
High-level [1]; generally easier to maintain [1], more portable [1], so less processor-specific rewriting is needed [1].
